loop_role: analysis turns raw code and compiler output into ranked, searchable, graph-shaped evidence the agent loop perceives with, plans against, and evolves from.

examples.title: Rank build errors before retrying a fix
examples.loop_role: Plugs into verify: after a compile/test tool result fails, feed stderr lines as RawError into ErrorAnalyzer::analyze_batch, then call first_to_fix to pick the single AnalyzedError with the lowest ErrorCategory::priority (TypeError=1 beats StyleWarning=30) so the next act stage patches the root cause, not the noisiest diagnostic.
examples.affects: Converts an unbounded compiler dump into one chosen AnalyzedError plus its FixSuggestion, shrinking the tool result that re-enters the context window and preventing the loop from burning budget fixing warnings while a type error still blocks the build.
examples.touch_ux: A red-to-amber stacked bar node; each segment is an AnalyzedError sorted by priority. Tap a segment to expand its FixSuggestion, long-press to pin it as the loop's current fix target, pinch out to see the full grouped list. Live badge shows error count by category, e.g. '3 type / 12 warn'.

examples.title: Gate auto-fixes on FixSuggestion confidence
examples.loop_role: Wires verify directly into act: only apply a FixSuggestion when auto_fixable is true and confidence clears a threshold (e.g. the 0.8 confidence dead_code suggestion from unused_code_suggestion); otherwise route the AnalyzedError back to plan so the model proposes the patch instead of blindly inserting fix_code.
examples.affects: Protects trust state — an applied auto-fix must be reported as 'deterministic suggestion applied' rather than model reasoning, and low-confidence suggestions stay as evidence annotations on the checkpoint instead of mutating the worktree.
examples.touch_ux: Small wrench glyph attached to each error node, filled green when auto_fixable && confidence >= 0.8, hollow otherwise. Tap applies the fix_code inline and flashes a diff edge to the checkpoint node; long-press shows the notes field; a hollow wrench refuses the tap with a shake.

examples.title: Compress compiler noise with group_by_category
examples.loop_role: Sits between act (cargo build tool call) and the next perceive: ErrorAnalyzer::group_by_category buckets AnalyzedError values by ErrorCategory so the loop re-ingests a histogram ('2 BorrowError, 8 UnusedWarning') instead of 200 raw lines, and summary() renders the one-paragraph digest that actually enters the context window.
examples.affects: Directly reduces context-window pressure from tool results: N raw diagnostics become ~10 category buckets, and the per-category priority order (TypeError=1 … StyleWarning=30) gives the planner a deterministic fix sequence without re-reading the log.
examples.touch_ux: A funnel node that visually swallows a scrolling raw-log edge and emits a tidy stack of category chips. Tap a chip to drill into that bucket's errors, pinch to collapse back to the histogram. Live badge: total error count and the top category name.

examples.title: Retrieve code lexically with BM25Index
examples.loop_role: Perceive-stage retrieval: cognitive/intelligence.rs already embeds BM25Index, so model it as the lexical half of context selection — add file symbols/snippets with add_batch, then search(query, limit) at plan time and inject only the top BM25Result hits into the prompt.
examples.affects: Bounds the context window by replacing whole-file reads with scored snippets; BM25Result.score also feeds evidence ranking so the planner can cite why a snippet was chosen. rebuild() after bulk add_batch keeps scores honest instead of stale.
examples.touch_ux: A magnifier node with a term-cloud halo sized by BM25 score. Edges flow from it to context-window node carrying ranked snippets. Tap a halo term to see matching documents, long-press a snippet edge to pin it into context, badge shows indexed doc count (len) and last query latency.

examples.title: Keep the BM25 index in sync with edits
examples.loop_role: Runs in the act→verify seam: whenever the loop writes a file, call BM25Index::remove for the old document id and add the new content (or remove_all + add_batch after multi-file patches) so the next perceive never retrieves pre-edit code as evidence.
examples.affects: Stale retrieval is a trust failure — the loop would plan against code that no longer exists. Incremental remove/add keeps evidence truthful without a full rebuild(), which matters for budget since rebuild recomputes all document frequencies.
examples.touch_ux: An index node with a freshness ring: green when in sync, amber pulsing while a pending edit edge hasn't been flushed into the index. Tap forces the remove/add flush, long-press triggers full rebuild. Badge shows 'docs: N, pending: M'.

examples.title: Fuse BM25 and vector hits for context packing
examples.loop_role: Perceive: run BM25Index::search and VectorIndex::search over the same query, merge by chunk id, and let ChunkType::weight (from vector_store) bias the fused ranking before handing a fixed-size bundle to plan — this is the retrieval core behind cognitive/rag.rs.
examples.affects: The fused, weighted top-k is what actually occupies the context window; a hard limit on k plus SearchFilter::with_min_score keeps the bundle inside the token budget and records each chosen chunk as scored evidence.
examples.touch_ux: Two rails (blue lexical, purple semantic) converging on a merger node; hit cards slide along each rail by score. Pinch zooms the fused ranking, drag a card to reorder priority manually. Badge shows fused count and min-score cutoff.

examples.title: Chunk Rust sources by symbol, not lines
examples.loop_role: Perceive-time ingestion: CodeChunker::chunk_rust splits files at fn/struct/impl boundaries producing CodeChunk values with ChunkMetadata (with_symbol, with_tag), so embeddings and BM25 documents align with the units the loop actually edits and cites.
examples.affects: Symbol-aligned chunks make tool results and evidence cite-able at fn granularity; ChunkType::weight lets Function chunks outrank Comment chunks when the context window is tight, and ChunkMetadata.symbol gives checkpoints stable anchors.
examples.touch_ux: A file node that splits like a pie into symbol slices when pinched open, each slice colored by ChunkType. Tap a slice previews the CodeChunk content, long-press re-chunks with a different max_chunk_size. Badge shows chunks per file and average chunk size.

examples.title: Filter retrieval before it touches the prompt
examples.loop_role: A perceive-stage valve: build a SearchFilter with with_file_pattern, with_language, with_chunk_type and with_min_score, and let SearchFilter::matches screen CodeChunk candidates so plan only sees in-scope, above-threshold evidence.
examples.affects: Protects both budget and trust: with_min_score drops weak matches that would otherwise pad the context window with noise, and file-pattern scoping keeps cross-project chunks (CollectionScope::Global) from leaking into project evidence.
examples.touch_ux: A sieve node on the retrieval edge with four dials (pattern, language, type, min score). Dragging the score dial animates chunks falling out of the stream. Tap the node to edit the filter, badge shows pass/drop counts live.

examples.title: Report index health instead of failing silently
examples.loop_role: Verify-stage self-check wired to the doctor path: run VectorIndex::check_health and verify_index_integrity after loading a persisted collection; on IndexHealth::Corrupt (NaN/Inf, dimension mismatch) trigger compact()/clear() + re-embed, on Degraded continue but annotate the trust state.
examples.affects: Honest status per the repo's review rules: a Degraded index must render an amber badge, never green, and the integrity issue strings become evidence attached to the session checkpoint so later stages know retrieval scores are suspect.
examples.touch_ux: A heart-monitor node on the vector store: green pulse for Healthy, amber arrhythmia for Degraded, flat red line for Corrupt. Tap lists the verify_index_integrity issue strings, long-press offers compact or rebuild. Badge shows health enum + issue count.

examples.title: Scope vector memory by lifetime
examples.loop_role: Remember stage: choose CollectionScope per VectorCollection — Project for repo knowledge persisted across runs (chunks are serde-persisted so RAG survives restarts), Session for scratch context cleared on restart, Global for cross-project patterns — so evolve and future sessions inherit only what should persist.
examples.affects: Controls what lands on the loop's memory objects: Project collections become durable evidence tied to the repo, Session collections keep the checkpoint small, and the serde-persisted chunks field with the skipped id-index (rebuild_id_index after load) defines exactly what survives a restart.
examples.touch_ux: Three stacked memory vaults (project = blue, session = ephemeral gray, global = purple). Dragging a chunk card between vaults changes its scope; session vault has a visible countdown-to-clear shimmer. Badge shows chunks per scope.

examples.title: Invalidate embeddings when files change
examples.loop_role: Act→remember hygiene: after the loop edits or deletes a file, call VectorCollection::remove_file to drop every chunk of that path before re-chunking and re-adding, guaranteeing the next perceive retrieves post-edit semantics only.
examples.affects: Prevents stale vector evidence from contaminating plan; remove_file keeps files() listings truthful, which downstream context budgeting relies on when projecting how much of the repo is actually indexed.
examples.touch_ux: Edited file node emits a red 'stale' pulse down its embedding edges; the chunks fade out as remove_file runs. Tap the file re-chunks immediately, long-press defers to batch. Badge: stale-chunk count awaiting invalidation.

examples.title: Trace change blast radius with find_path
examples.loop_role: Plan stage: build a CodeGraph via GraphBuilder (add_function, add_call, add_import) and use CodeGraph::find_path plus dependencies()/dependents() from a target GraphNode to enumerate what an edit can break, feeding that list into the plan's verify checklist.
examples.affects: The path of node ids becomes structured evidence attached to the plan, and its length calibrates verify budget — a 6-hop dependent chain justifies running more tests than a leaf node. subgraph() on the path bounds the context to the affected region.
examples.touch_ux: Graph canvas nodes use NodeType::color and dot_shape directly (already render-ready). find_path animates a glowing route between two tapped nodes; pinch collapses to subgraph of the path. Badge: hop count and dependents count.

examples.title: Detect dependency cycles during evolution
examples.loop_role: Evolve stage: run CodeGraph::find_cycles over the workspace graph after large refactors; each returned cycle of node ids is evidence that module boundaries degraded, and clearing a cycle becomes a measurable evolution goal across checkpoints.
examples.affects: Cycle count is a checkpoint-level metric: store it per session so the loop can show trend (evolve claims must be measured, not estimated). New cycles introduced by the loop's own edits should block the 'improved structure' trust claim.
examples.touch_ux: Cycles render as red closed loops threading through graph nodes; the loop literally looks like a loop. Tap a cycle lists its member nodes, long-press pins 'break this cycle' as an evolution goal. Badge: cycle count with up/down trend arrow.

examples.title: Spot hub files with node_metrics
examples.loop_role: Perceive→plan risk lens: CodeGraph::node_metrics computes NodeMetrics (in/out degree) per node and find_hubs(threshold) surfaces over-connected files, so the planner treats edits to hubs as high-blast-radius and schedules extra verify steps.
examples.affects: Hub scores become a risk multiplier on the plan's budget: touching a hub node raises the required test evidence before a checkpoint can be marked verified, and hubs get priority placement in the context window since their code affects many dependents.
examples.touch_ux: Hub nodes grow physically larger and gain a gravity effect that pulls edges taut — the canvas makes centrality tactile. Tap shows NodeMetrics numbers, long-press extracts the hub's subgraph for focused editing. Badge: max in-degree and hub count at current threshold.

examples.title: Render graphs the canvas can display natively
examples.loop_role: Presentation layer of perceive: GraphRenderer::render with OutputFormat (Dot/Mermaid) plus EdgeType::mermaid_arrow and NodeType::dot_shape means the analysis module already emits view-ready syntax — the touch canvas should consume the same CodeGraph and share its color/shape vocabulary instead of inventing a parallel one.
examples.affects: Keeps the visual layer honest: what the user touches is the same GraphNode/GraphEdge data the loop reasons over, with with_meta key-values available as node tooltips and with_weight driving edge thickness — no lossy translation between evidence and display.
examples.touch_ux: This is the canvas substrate itself: nodes colored via NodeType::color, edges styled via EdgeType::dot_style, clusters via GraphRenderer::cluster. Two-finger tap toggles Mermaid source view, long-press a node reveals its with_doc string. Badge: node_count / edge_count.

examples.title: Open sessions with a workspace graph summary
examples.loop_role: Session-start perceive: build_workspace_graph with WorkspaceGraphOptions over the repo root, then summarize_graph to get a WorkspaceGraphSummary — the loop's first context artifact is a measured map of files/modules/functions, not a guess.
examples.affects: The summary is cheap, high-signal context: it seeds the planner with real structure counts and gives render_workspace_graph output for the user's canvas, while the full CodeGraph stays out of the prompt until subgraph() excerpts are needed — a clean budget split.
examples.touch_ux: The canvas home screen: a constellation of module nodes laid out from the workspace graph. Pinch zooms summary → module → symbol, tap a module runs subgraph to focus. Badge shows the WorkspaceGraphSummary counts (files, nodes, edges).

examples.title: Score tech debt by compounding interest
examples.loop_role: Evolve-stage input: represent each known shortcut as a DebtItem with DebtType (whose default_interest_rate varies per type) and DebtSeverity::multiplier, then use priority_score (fix_cost vs total_cost with monthly_interest) so the loop can argue with numbers which debt to pay next.
examples.affects: DebtItems become first-class objects on the loop's backlog: monthly_interest makes deferral cost visible per checkpoint, and DebtMetrics::calculate over all items gives a session-level debt figure that evolution reports must quote rather than hand-wave.
examples.touch_ux: Debt nodes shaped as weighted anchors dragging on their file nodes, sized by priority_score and colored by DebtSeverity. Tap shows fix_cost/total_cost/monthly_interest breakdown, long-press promotes to a sprint goal. Badge: total debt hours and monthly interest.

examples.title: Order the backlog with DebtPrioritizer
examples.loop_role: Plan stage for maintenance work: DebtTracker::prioritize with a chosen PrioritizationStrategy turns the DebtItem pile into an ordered Vec<PrioritizedItem>, and critical_items() flags anything the loop should fix before adding features.
examples.affects: The prioritized list is explicit plan evidence — each PrioritizedItem carries its rank rationale, so when the loop claims 'highest-impact fix first' that claim is checkable against the strategy, supporting honest status reporting.
examples.touch_ux: A sortable kanban rail of debt cards; switching PrioritizationStrategy animates cards re-ranking. Drag to override order manually (override is recorded, not silent). Tap a card shows its score components. Badge: strategy name + critical item count.

examples.title: Generate a payback-bounded refactoring roadmap
examples.loop_role: Bridges evolve and long-horizon plan: RoadmapGenerator::generate (with_max_hours capping each RoadmapPhase) turns PrioritizedItems into a RefactoringRoadmap whose payback_months and per-phase roi() tell the loop when to stop — a phase with negative ROI shouldn't be scheduled.
examples.affects: RoadmapPhases map naturally onto checkpoints: each phase is a verifiable unit with its own item set, and payback_months gives the trust state a concrete claim ('this roadmap pays back in N months') that can be re-measured as debt items close.
examples.touch_ux: A horizontal timeline of phase beads, each bead's size = hours, color = ROI (green positive, red negative). Swipe between phases, tap to expand its DebtItems, pinch to see payback_months projection curve. Badge: total phases and payback months.

examples.title: Correlate churn with debt to find hotspots
examples.loop_role: Evolve/perceive risk radar: feed git-derived FileStats into ChurnAnalyzer::add_file and debts into add_debt, then use hotspots(limit), correlate_churn_debt and correlate_age_debt so the loop verifies hardest where churn_rate × hotspot_score says bugs cluster, and generate_report emits the ChurnReport as session evidence.
examples.affects: CorrelationResult coefficients (with sample_size, so weak correlations are visibly weak) steer verify budget toward high-churn/high-debt files; the ChurnReport attached to a checkpoint makes 'we hardened the riskiest files' a measured claim rather than a vibe.
examples.touch_ux: A heat overlay on the file canvas: FileStats nodes glow by hotspot_score, with instability_index shown as flicker intensity. Tap a hot file shows churn_rate and the correlation coefficient, long-press schedules a hardening task. Badge: top hotspot path + correlation r value with sample size.
